question: In its reply of 8 May 2026 to written question E-000892/20261, the Commission comments on the maintenance of the Nord Stream pipelines. In its interpretative guidance of 23 January 2026, the Commission states that mere surveillance and monitoring of the pipelines’ status that is not connected to restoration and preservation of their functional condition does not fall under the transaction ban, whilst inspections aimed at restoring or maintaining their functional condition may be covered. 1.

Does the prohibition in Article 5af of Council Regulation (EU) No 833/2014 concerning restrictive measures in view of Russia’s actions destabilising the situation in Ukraine, as inserted by Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1494 of 18 July 2025 (18th sanctions package), also cover pipeline inspection and survey voyages which do not constitute maintenance but serve exclusively to ascertain the condition of the damaged pipelines?

On the basis of which verifiable criteria should this distinction be drawn in individual cases, in particular in the case of integrity inspections using remotely operated underwater vehicles, the results of which may serve both to avert danger and to facilitate subsequent repair?
answer: Article 5af of Council Regulation (EU) No 833/2014 prohibits EU operators from engaging in transactions in connection with the Nord Stream and Nord Stream 2 pipelines with regard to their completion, operation, maintenance or use. It also prohibits any transaction in connection with the financing concerning the completion, operation, maintenance or use of the pipelines.

Inspections are addressed by a frequently asked questions document (1), to clarify that those services aimed at the restoration or preservation of the functional condition of the pipeline, fall into the scope of the transaction ban. As explained therein, surveillance and monitoring unrelated to restoration and preservation of their functional condition (e.g.
surveillance and monitoring of facilities, premises and hardware for security purposes) do not fall under the transaction ban. Individual cases must be assessed by the national competent authorities.

Article 5af contemplates exceptions, as well as the possibility for national competent authorities to authorise certain transactions, notably for regular maintenance services which are strictly necessary to prevent environmental and safety risks or a negative impact on the fisheries sector.
